touches.text: Routes from authored stacks beside the code: providers (cost, connection), models (names, parameters, scores), combos (which pairs route).

Machine: route, the sieves (enabled, never_routed, serves_kind, keyed, addressed) built with the nest machine (16.2), cheapest survivor first. Nests are how the inference proxy resolves its routing questions. [Q#82: The nest shakes once and scores 0 or 1 (16.2), so one shake can pick the cheapest survivor but cannot order the rest; the walk that dials the next rung when a host is unreachable needs that order, and today route sorts it after the shake. Should the cheapest postprocess sieve pick one rung, and a host that does not answer send the walk back to route for a fresh shake with that rung left out by a sieve? (CC's recommendation: yes.)]
TOOLS: base, import_sieve; database client. MACHINES: route, nest.
A machine made of sieve tools. Each question is a sieve; sieves can come after others. Bands are phases: preprocess, measure, postprocess.
Sieves measure, never judge: deterministic Python.
USERS: the inference proxy, through its route machine (11.4.6); build_inspector (9.4.3).
